problems.title: Create & Traverse Linked List
problems.titleHi: Linked List Banao aur Traverse Karo

description.en: Given n elements, create a singly linked list and print all elements separated by spaces.
description.hi: N elements diye hain, ek singly linked list banao aur saare elements space se separate karke print karo.

explanation.en: Create list with 1->2->3->4->5, then traverse and print each node
explanation.hi: 1->2->3->4->5 wali list banao, phir traverse karke har node print karo

hints.en: Create a head node, then keep adding new nodes at the tail
hints.hi: Head node banao, phir tail pe naye nodes add karte jao

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
# Create and traverse linked list

approach.en: Create head with first element, then iterate and add remaining elements at tail. Traverse from head to NULL printing each node.
approach.hi: Pehle element se head banao, phir baaki elements ko tail pe add karo. Head se NULL tak traverse karke har node print karo.

code.python:
head = Node(arr[0])
tail = head
for i in range(1, n):
    tail.next = Node(arr[i])
    tail = tail.next
result = []
temp = head
while temp:
    result.append(str(temp.data))
    temp = temp.next
print(' '.join(result))

description.en: Given a linked list of n elements, insert a new element at the beginning and print the resulting list.
description.hi: N elements ki linked list diye hain, ek naya element beginning mein insert karo aur resulting list print karo.

explanation.hi: [2,3,4,5] ke beginning mein 1 insert karo to [1,2,3,4,5] milega

hints.en: Create new node, point its next to current head, update head to new node
hints.hi: Naya node banao, uska next current head ko point karo, head ko naye node pe update karo

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
val = int(input())
# Insert val at beginning and print

approach.en: Create the linked list from input, then create a new node with the given value and set its next to current head. The new node becomes the head.
approach.hi: Input se linked list banao, phir given value ka naya node banao aur uska next current head pe set karo. Naya node head ban jayega.

code.python:
head = Node(arr[0])
tail = head
for i in range(1, n):
    tail.next = Node(arr[i])
    tail = tail.next
new_node = Node(val)
new_node.next = head
head = new_node
result = []
temp = head
while temp:
    result.append(str(temp.data))
    temp = temp.next
print(' '.join(result))

description.en: Given a linked list and a value, delete the first occurrence of that value and print the resulting list. If the value is not found, print the original list.
description.hi: Linked list aur ek value diye hain, us value ka pehla occurrence delete karo aur resulting list print karo. Agar value nahi mili to original list print karo.

explanation.en: Delete node with value 3 from the list
explanation.hi: List se value 3 wala node delete karo

hints.en: Handle head deletion separately. For other nodes, find the previous node and skip the target.
hints.hi: Head deletion alag handle karo. Baaki nodes ke liye previous node dhundho aur target ko skip karo.

description.en: Given a singly linked list, reverse it and print the reversed list.
description.hi: Singly linked list diye hain, use reverse karo aur reversed list print karo.

hints.en: Use three pointers: prev, curr, next. Reverse the direction of each pointer.
hints.hi: Teen pointers use karo: prev, curr, next. Har pointer ki direction ulta karo.

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
# Reverse linked list and print

approach.en: Use iterative approach with prev, curr, next pointers. At each step, reverse curr's pointer to prev, then advance all three pointers.
approach.hi: Iterative approach use karo prev, curr, next pointers ke saath. Har step pe curr ka pointer prev ki taraf reverse karo, phir teeno pointers ko aage badhao.

code.python:
head = Node(arr[0])
tail = head
for i in range(1, n):
    tail.next = Node(arr[i])
    tail = tail.next
prev = None
curr = head
while curr:
    nxt = curr.next
    curr.next = prev
    prev = curr
    curr = nxt
head = prev
result = []
temp = head
while temp:
    result.append(str(temp.data))
    temp = temp.next
print(' '.join(result))

description.en: Given a singly linked list, find and print the middle element. If the list has even number of nodes, return the second middle node.
description.hi: Singly linked list diye hain, middle element dhundho aur print karo. Agar list mein even number of nodes hain, to second middle node return karo.

explanation.hi: Even length ke liye second middle: [1,2,3,4,5,6] -> 4

hints.en: Use slow and fast pointer technique. Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. When fast reaches end, slow is at middle.
hints.hi: Slow aur fast pointer technique use karo. Slow 1 step, fast 2 steps. Jab fast end pe pahunche, slow middle pe hoga.

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
# Find middle element

approach.en: Use Floyd's slow-fast pointer. Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. When fast reaches NULL or last node, slow points to the middle.
approach.hi: Floyd's slow-fast pointer use karo. Slow 1 step, fast 2 steps. Jab fast NULL ya last node pe pahunchta hai, slow middle pe point karta hai.

code.python:
head = Node(arr[0])
tail = head
for i in range(1, n):
    tail.next = Node(arr[i])
    tail = tail.next
slow = fast = head
while fast and fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
print(slow.data)

problems.title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
problems.titleHi: Linked List mein Cycle Detect Karo

description.en: Given a linked list, determine if it has a cycle. The input gives n nodes and a position pos (0-indexed) where the tail connects to. If pos is -1, there is no cycle. Print 'true' if cycle exists, 'false' otherwise.
description.hi: Linked list diye hain, check karo usme cycle hai ya nahi. Input mein n nodes hain aur ek position pos (0-indexed) jahan tail connect hota hai. Agar pos -1 hai to cycle nahi hai. Cycle hai to 'true' print karo, nahi to 'false'.

explanation.en: Tail connects to node at index 1 (value 2), forming a cycle
explanation.hi: Tail index 1 pe (value 2) connect hota hai, cycle ban jaata hai
Koi cycle nahi hai, pos -1 hai

hints.en: Use Floyd's cycle detection: slow pointer moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. If they meet, cycle exists.
hints.hi: Floyd's cycle detection use karo: slow 1 step, fast 2 steps. Agar milte hain to cycle hai.

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
pos = int(input())
# Detect cycle

approach.en: Build the list and create cycle if pos >= 0. Use Floyd's algorithm with slow (1 step) and fast (2 steps) pointers. If they meet, cycle exists.
approach.hi: List banao aur agar pos >= 0 hai to cycle banao. Floyd's algorithm use karo slow (1 step) aur fast (2 steps) pointers ke saath. Agar milte hain to cycle hai.

code.python:
nodes = [Node(x) for x in arr]
for i in range(n-1):
    nodes[i].next = nodes[i+1]
if pos >= 0:
    nodes[-1].next = nodes[pos]
head = nodes[0]
slow = fast = head
cycle = False
while fast and fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
    if slow == fast:
        cycle = True
        break
print('true' if cycle else 'false')

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Linked Lists
problems.titleHi: Do Sorted Linked Lists Merge Karo

description.en: Given two sorted linked lists, merge them into a single sorted linked list and print the result.
description.hi: Do sorted linked lists diye hain, unhe ek single sorted linked list mein merge karo aur result print karo.

constraints: Lists are sorted in ascending order

hints.en: Use a dummy node. Compare heads of both lists, attach smaller one and advance that pointer.
hints.hi: Dummy node use karo. Dono lists ke heads compare karo, chhota wala attach karo aur us pointer ko aage badhao.

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr1 = list(map(int, input().split())) if n > 0 else []
m = int(input())
arr2 = list(map(int, input().split())) if m > 0 else []
# Merge two sorted lists

approach.en: Create a dummy node. Iterate both lists, always picking the smaller head and advancing that pointer. Attach remaining nodes at end.
approach.hi: Dummy node banao. Dono lists iterate karo, hamesha chhota head pick karo aur us pointer ko aage badhao. End mein bache hue nodes attach karo.

code.python:
def build(arr):
    if not arr: return None
    head = Node(arr[0])
    tail = head
    for x in arr[1:]:
        tail.next = Node(x)
        tail = tail.next
    return head
h1, h2 = build(arr1), build(arr2)
dummy = Node(0)
tail = dummy
while h1 and h2:
    if h1.data <= h2.data:
        tail.next = h1; h1 = h1.next
    else:
        tail.next = h2; h2 = h2.next
    tail = tail.next
tail.next = h1 if h1 else h2
result = []
temp = dummy.next
while temp:
    result.append(str(temp.data))
    temp = temp.next
print(' '.join(result))

description.en: Given a linked list, remove the nth node from the end and print the resulting list.
description.hi: Linked list diye hain, end se nth node hatao aur resulting list print karo.

explanation.en: Remove 3rd from end which is the head
explanation.hi: End se 3rd hatao jo head hai

hints.en: Use two pointers: move fast pointer n steps ahead, then move both until fast reaches end. Slow's next is the target.
hints.hi: Do pointers use karo: fast ko n steps aage bhejo, phir dono ko chalao jab tak fast end pe na pahunch jaye. Slow ka next target hai.

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
k = int(input())
# Remove kth from end

approach.en: Use a dummy node before head. Move fast k steps ahead, then move both slow and fast until fast reaches the last node. Now slow->next is the target node to remove.
approach.hi: Head se pehle dummy node use karo. Fast ko k steps aage bhejo, phir slow aur fast dono ko chalao jab tak fast last node pe na pahunch jaye. Ab slow->next target node hai jise remove karna hai.

code.python:
head = Node(arr[0])
tail = head
for i in range(1, n):
    tail.next = Node(arr[i])
    tail = tail.next
dummy = Node(0)
dummy.next = head
fast = slow = dummy
for _ in range(k):
    fast = fast.next
while fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next
slow.next = slow.next.next
head = dummy.next
result = []
temp = head
while temp:
    result.append(str(temp.data))
    temp = temp.next
print(' '.join(result))

description.en: Given a singly linked list, check if it is a palindrome. Print 'true' if it is, 'false' otherwise.
description.hi: Singly linked list diye hain, check karo wo palindrome hai ya nahi. Agar hai to 'true' print karo, nahi to 'false'.

explanation.hi: 1->2->3->2->1 aage se aur peeche se same padhte hain

hints.en: Find the middle using slow-fast pointer, reverse the second half, then compare both halves
hints.hi: Slow-fast pointer se middle dhundho, second half reverse karo, phir dono halves compare karo

starterCode.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
# Check if palindrome

approach.en: Find middle with slow-fast pointers, reverse second half, compare first and second halves node by node.
approach.hi: Slow-fast pointers se middle dhundho, second half reverse karo, dono halves ko node by node compare karo.

code.python:
head = Node(arr[0])
tail = head
for i in range(1, n):
    tail.next = Node(arr[i])
    tail = tail.next
# Find middle
slow = fast = head
while fast and fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
# Reverse second half
prev = None
curr = slow
while curr:
    nxt = curr.next
    curr.next = prev
    prev = curr
    curr = nxt
# Compare
l, r = head, prev
pal = True
while r:
    if l.data != r.data:
        pal = False
        break
    l = l.next
    r = r.next
print('true' if pal else 'false')

description.en: You are given a linked list where each node has a next pointer and a bottom pointer. Each bottom pointer leads to a sorted sub-list. Flatten the list into a single sorted linked list using bottom pointers. Print the flattened sorted list.
description.hi: Ek linked list diye hain jisme har node ka next pointer aur bottom pointer hai. Har bottom pointer ek sorted sub-list ki taraf jaata hai. List ko ek single sorted linked list mein flatten karo bottom pointers use karke. Flattened sorted list print karo.

explanation.en: Merge all sorted sub-lists into one sorted list: 5->7->8->10->19->20->22->28->30->35->40->45
explanation.hi: Saari sorted sub-lists ko ek sorted list mein merge karo: 5->7->8->10->19->20->22->28->30->35->40->45

hints.en: Start from the last two sub-lists, merge them. Then merge result with the third-last, and so on.
hints.hi: Last do sub-lists se shuru karo, unhe merge karo. Phir result ko third-last ke saath merge karo, aur aage bhi aise hi.

hints.en: This is like merging k sorted lists. You can use the merge function from merge sort repeatedly.
hints.hi: Ye k sorted lists merge karne jaisa hai. Merge sort ka merge function baar baar use kar sakte ho.

approach.en: Use merge function from merge sort. Start from the rightmost two lists, merge them, then merge the result with the next list moving left. Repeat until all lists are merged into one sorted list.
approach.hi: Merge sort ka merge function use karo. Rightmost do lists se shuru karo, merge karo, phir result ko next list ke saath merge karo left ki taraf. Repeat karo jab tak saari lists ek sorted list mein merge na ho jaayein.

code.python:
def merge(a, b):
    if not a: return b
    if not b: return a
    if a.data <= b.data:
        result = a
        result.bottom = merge(a.bottom, b)
    else:
        result = b
        result.bottom = merge(a, b.bottom)
    result.next = None
    return result

def flatten(head):
    if not head or not head.next:
        return head
    head.next = flatten(head.next)
    head = merge(head, head.next)
    return head

# Call flatten(head) and print using bottom pointers
node = flatten(head)
result = []
while node:
    result.append(str(node.data))
    node = node.bottom
print(' '.join(result))

solution.timeComplexity: O(n * m) where n is number of sub-lists, m is average length
